title: Cloudline Hiring
source: Synthetic case written for this project; free to use and commit.
public_brief: Cloudline, a 60-person cloud-infrastructure startup, has extended a verbal offer to a senior software engineer. The recruiter and the candidate are meeting to settle the remaining terms of the written offer: base salary, signing bonus, remote days per week, start date, and vacation days. Both sides want to reach an agreement today if they can.

roles.name: Candidate
roles.confidential_brief: You are a senior engineer with a competing offer from a larger company that you would take if this negotiation fails. You care most about salary and being able to work remotely: you have a long commute and a young child. The signing bonus is nice but matters less to you. You need about four weeks to hand off your current project; starting in two weeks would burn bridges with your current team, and eight weeks would delay your next paycheck uncomfortably.

roles.name: Cloudline Recruiter
roles.confidential_brief: You are Cloudline's head of talent. The founders want this hire but cash is tight before the next funding round, so a signing bonus is painful: it comes straight out of this quarter's runway. Salary matters but is easier to justify to the board. Cloudline is quietly moving to a remote-friendly policy, so remote days cost you little. A major project kicks off in four weeks and you would love the new hire there for it; eight weeks would mean missing the kickoff. If this fails you would fall back to a slower search with a recruiting agency.
